response_text:
# Spring Break Family Road Trip: Seattle → San Antonio → Austin → Houston

## Complete Trip Plan | April 10–18

---

## 1. Rental Car Recommendation

### Best Category: **Mid-Size SUV (e.g., Toyota RAV4, Ford Escape, or similar)**

A mid-size SUV is the sweet spot for your family of 4. You'll have enough cargo space for luggage, snacks, coolers, and kid gear without paying the premium for a full-size SUV. The higher seating position also makes the Texas highway driving more comfortable, and fuel economy stays reasonable (28–32 mpg highway).

### Estimated Cost

| Detail | Info |
|---|---|
| **Pickup** | SAT Airport, April 10 (afternoon) |
| **Drop-off** | HOU (Hobby Airport), April 17 evening or April 18 early morning |
| **Duration** | 7–8 days |
| **Estimated cost** | **$350–$500** total (including taxes and fees) |

> **Note on drop-off location:** Drop off at **HOU (Hobby)** rather than IAH (George Bush Intercontinental) since your return flight departs from HOU. This also saves you from dealing with Houston traffic between airports on the morning of your flight. If you drop off the evening of April 17, you could stay at a hotel near Hobby and walk/shuttle to the terminal on the 18th.

### Tips for the Best Rental Car Deals

- **Book through Costco Travel** if you have a membership — they consistently offer competitive rates with no cancellation fees, and they bundle in a second driver free.
- **Compare on AutoSlash.com** — this site applies coupon codes automatically and will email you if prices drop after you book.
- **Check Turo** as an alternative — sometimes private car owners offer SUVs at lower rates, though airport pickup can be slightly less convenient.
- **Avoid prepaying** unless the cancellation terms are flexible; rental car prices in Texas tend to fluctuate and often drop closer to the date.
- **Decline the rental company's insurance** if your personal auto insurance or credit card (Chase Sapphire, Amex, etc.) already provides collision/loss damage coverage. Call your insurer before the trip to confirm.
- **Fill up gas before returning the car** — rental companies charge 2–3× the pump price for fuel if you return it less than full.
- **One-way drop-off fees:** SAT → HOU one-way rentals are common in Texas and many companies (especially Enterprise, National, and Hertz) waive or minimize the one-way fee on this corridor. When comparing quotes, make sure the total you see includes any one-way surcharge.

---

## 2. Hotel Recommendations

### San Antonio — 3 Nights (April 10–13)

You want to be near the **Riverwalk** because it's the heart of family-friendly San Antonio — restaurants, boat tours, and the Alamo are all within walking distance. Being centrally located also means you won't need to drive (and pay for parking) during your San Antonio days.

---

#### Option A: **Drury Inn & Suites San Antonio Riverwalk**

| Detail | Info |
|---|---|
| **Price** | ~$160–$200/night |
| **3-night total** | ~$480–$600 |
| **Location** | 1 block from the Riverwalk, 5-minute walk to the Alamo |

**Pros:**
- Complimentary full hot breakfast every morning (eggs, biscuits, waffles — genuinely good, not just muffins and coffee) — this alone saves your family $40–$50/day on breakfast
- Complimentary "5:30 Kickback" every evening: free hot food, beer, wine, and soft drinks for 90 minutes — essentially a free light dinner
- Indoor/outdoor pool and a rooftop pool with views of downtown
- Consistently rated one of the best family-value hotels in San Antonio
- Free Wi-Fi, parking available (though there's a fee at this location, ~$20–$28/night for self-parking)

**Cons:**
- Books up quickly for Spring Break — reserve ASAP
- Rooms are clean and comfortable but not luxurious; decor is functional
- The evening kickback can get crowded during peak season

**Why it's great for your family:** The included breakfast and evening food/drinks could save you $100+/day on dining. The pool will be a hit with an 8 and 11-year-old after long days of sightseeing. Drury is a Midwest-based chain that has quietly built a cult following among road-tripping families for exactly this value proposition.

---

#### Option B: **Holiday Inn San Antonio Riverwalk**

| Detail | Info |
|---|---|
| **Price** | ~$150–$190/night |
| **3-night total** | ~$450–$570 |
| **Location** | Directly on the Riverwalk |

**Pros:**
- Right on the Riverwalk — you walk out the back door and you're on it
- Outdoor pool
- Kids eat free program (kids 12 and under eat free from the hotel restaurant's kids' menu when accompanied by an adult ordering an entrée)
- Familiar brand, IHG rewards eligible
- Rooms are recently updated at this location

**Cons:**
- Breakfast is not included (unless you have IHG elite status)
- Riverwalk-facing rooms can pick up noise from restaurants and bars, especially on weekend evenings — request a courtyard-facing or upper-floor room
- Parking is valet only, ~$30–$38/night

**Why it's great for your family:** The location is unbeatable — no navigating with tired kids after dinner because you're steps from your room. The kids-eat-free benefit offsets the lack of free breakfast somewhat.

---

#### Option C: **Hyatt Place San Antonio Riverwalk (Budget-Friendlier)**

| Detail | Info |
|---|---|
| **Price** | ~$130–$170/night |
| **3-night total** | ~$390–$510 |
| **Location** | 2–3 blocks from the Riverwalk |

**Pros:**
- Complimentary breakfast (a step above continental — hot items included)
- Spacious rooms with a separate living area and pull-out sofa (great for families — kids get their own sleeping space)
- Outdoor pool
- Slightly lower price point than the options directly on the Riverwalk
- Free Wi-Fi, World of Hyatt points eligible

**Cons:**
- Not directly on the Riverwalk — you'll walk 5–10 minutes to reach it
- Self-parking is ~$22–$28/night
- The immediate surrounding blocks aren't as scenic as being right on the river

**Why it's great for your family:** The room layout is the standout — having a separate couch/living area means the adults can stay up after the kids fall asleep without whispering in the dark. The included breakfast saves money every morning.

---

**My recommendation:** **Drury Inn & Suites** is the best overall value for a family on a budget. The included breakfast AND evening kickback are game-changers. At roughly $500 for 3 nights with two meals/day effectively covered, nothing else comes close on value.

---

### Austin — 4 Nights (April 13–17)

You want to be walkable to **South Congress (SoCo)** or **downtown**. South Congress is Austin's most family-friendly walkable strip — food trailers, quirky shops, the famous "I love you so much" and "Greetings from Austin" murals, and ice cream shops. Downtown puts you closer to museums and the Congress Avenue Bridge (bats!).

---

#### Option A: **Hampton Inn & Suites Austin-Downtown/Convention Center**

| Detail | Info |
|---|---|
| **Price** | ~$160–$210/night |
| **4-night total** | ~$640–$840 |
| **Location** | Downtown, ~10-minute walk to South Congress bridge, close to 6th Street and convention center area |

**Pros:**
- Complimentary hot breakfast (Hilton's Hampton breakfast is solid — waffles, eggs, oatmeal, fruit)
- Outdoor pool
- Walking distance to the Congress Avenue Bridge for the bat colony
- Walkable to multiple restaurants and the Rainey Street district (which also has some family-friendly food options during daytime)
- Hilton Honors points eligible
- Self-parking available (~$25–$35/night)

**Cons:**
- Downtown Austin on weekend nights can be noisy (6th Street bar district is nearby) — request a room on a higher floor away from the street
- Not directly on South Congress — it's a 15–20 minute walk across the bridge to SoCo, which is very doable but not "step outside and you're there"
- Rooms are standard Hampton — comfortable, clean, but not unique

**Why it's great for your family:** Breakfast included, pool for the kids, and a central location that lets you walk to multiple attractions without constantly driving and parking. Solid, reliable, family-friendly.

---

#### Option B: **Hotel San José (South Congress — Boutique Option)**

| Detail | Info |
|---|---|
| **Price** | ~$200–$280/night |
| **4-night total** | ~$800–$1,120 |
| **Location** | Right on South Congress Avenue |

**Pros:**
- Iconic Austin boutique hotel — it *is* the SoCo experience
- Minimalist, beautiful courtyard with a small pool
- You're steps from SoCo's best shops, food trucks, and murals
- A genuinely unique, "only in Austin" place to stay — your older kid especially might think it's cool

**Cons:**
- Small rooms — this is a converted 1930s motor court; rooms are stylish but compact, and there's no room for a rollaway bed in most configurations
- No breakfast included
- No kids' amenities to speak of — this is more of an aesthetic boutique hotel, not a family-resort vibe
- At the higher end, it pushes your budget significantly
- Parking is limited and costs extra

**Why it's great for your family:** If you want the quintessential Austin experience and your family is comfortable with a smaller, more intimate hotel, this is unforgettable. However, it's the least practical choice for families — I include it because the location is perfect and some families love the vibe.

---

#### Option C: **Staybridge Suites Austin South (Budget-Friendlier)**

| Detail | Info |
|---|---|
| **Price** | ~$120–$160/night |
| **4-night total** | ~$480–$640 |
| **Location** | South Austin, ~5-minute drive to South Congress, ~10 minutes to downtown |

**Pros:**
- Full kitchen in every suite — you can cook breakfast and some dinners, potentially saving hundreds on food
- Complimentary hot breakfast
- Evening social (free light snacks and drinks) on select evenings (usually Tue/Wed/Thu)
- Significantly more space than a standard hotel room — separate living and sleeping areas
- Outdoor pool, guest laundry, free parking
- IHG rewards eligible

**Cons:**
- Not walkable to South Congress or downtown — you'll need to drive and park
- Located in a more suburban commercial area — not as charming or "Austin-y"
- You lose the spontaneity of being able to walk to restaurants and attractions

**Why it's great for your family:** This is the budget play. Four nights with included breakfast, a full kitchen, free parking, and more space for under $600? That's hard to beat. The tradeoff is that you'll drive everywhere, but parking in South Austin isn't nearly as painful as downtown.

---

**My recommendation:** **Hampton Inn Downtown** strikes the best balance of location, value, and family-friendliness. If budget is tight, the **Staybridge Suites** saves real money, especially if you use the kitchen for a few meals. I'd lean Hampton for this trip because being able to walk to things in Austin is a huge quality-of-life upgrade with kids — fewer "everybody get in the car" moments.

---

## 3. Day-by-Day Itinerary

---

### SAN ANTONIO

---

### 📅 April 10 (Thursday) — Arrival Day

**Theme: Easy landing, good food, low-key exploring**

| Time | Activity |
|---|---|
| **~2:00–3:00 PM** | Land at SAT, pick up rental car. Grab the car seats/boosters you reserved. Load up. |
| **3:00–4:00 PM** | Drive to hotel (~15–20 min from airport), check in, freshen up. Let the kids decompress — travel is tiring. |
| **4:30–5:30 PM** | **Walk the Riverwalk.** Start with a gentle stroll. The San Antonio Riverwalk is one level below street level, lined with cypress trees, restaurants, and stone bridges. It's magical as the late afternoon light comes in. Let the kids lead the pace — there's no agenda, just wander. The walk from most Riverwalk hotels to the Alamo and back is about 1–1.5 miles and totally flat. |
| **5:30–6:00 PM** | **See the Alamo from outside.** It's right at street level at the north end of the Riverwalk. You won't go inside tonight (save that for tomorrow), but the kids can see it and you can explain what it is. It's smaller than most people expect, which is its own conversation starter: "This tiny building is where 200 people tried to hold off thousands." |
| **6:00–7:00 PM** | **Dinner on the Riverwalk.** Family-friendly picks: **Casa Rio** (the oldest restaurant on the Riverwalk — Tex-Mex, colorful umbrellas, right on the water, kids' menu, expect $60–$80 for a family of 4) or **Iron Cactus** (slightly more upscale Tex-Mex with a great kids' menu and riverside patio). |
| **7:30 PM** | **Rio San Antonio Cruise** (optional if kids have energy). A 35-minute narrated boat ride along the Riverwalk. Tickets are ~$15/adult and ~$5/child (under 5 free, 6–12 discounted). The boats run until 9 PM, and the Riverwalk is beautifully lit at night. This is a perfect "sit and relax" activity for tired-but-not-ready-for-bed kids. |
| **8:30 PM** | Back to hotel. Pool time if the kids catch a second wind. Bedtime. |

> **Pro tip:** If you're staying at the Drury, you arrive just in time for the 5:30 Kickback — free food and drinks for the whole family. Eat there, then walk the Riverwalk after. That saves you dinner costs on night one.

---

### 📅 April 11 (Friday) — Big San Antonio Day

**Theme: History, culture, animals**

| Time | Activity |
|---|---|
| **7:30–8:30 AM** | Breakfast at hotel (free if you chose Drury or Hyatt Place). |
| **9:00–10:30 AM** | **The Alamo & Alamo Gardens.** Now you go inside. The Alamo itself is free to enter (timed tickets are required — **book online in advance at thealamo.org**). The new museum (opened 2024/2025) adds excellent context with artifacts and interactive exhibits. Budget about 90 minutes. For the 11-year-old, the history is fascinating; for the 8-year-old, the cannons and weapons displays hold attention. Talk about what it meant, why people fought — it's a real teaching moment. |
| **10:30–11:00 AM** | Walk to the **San Antonio Museum of Art** or drive to the next activity (depending on your family's museum tolerance). |
| **11:00 AM–2:00 PM** | **San Fernando Cathedral & Market Square (El Mercado).** San Fernando Cathedral is the oldest cathedral in Texas (free to enter, stunning inside, 5-minute visit). Then walk 2 blocks to **Market Square**, the largest Mexican market outside Mexico. Kids love browsing the colorful stalls (piñatas, maracas, painted pottery). Grab lunch here at **Mi Tierra Café & Bakery** — it's been open since 1941, is decorated like a permanent fiesta, has a massive bakery counter, and is an institution. Expect to spend ~$50–$65 for a family of 4. The wait can be long, but it moves fast — put your name in and browse the bakery/market while you wait. |
| **2:30–5:30 PM** | **San Antonio Zoo** OR **Natural Bridge Caverns** (choose one). See activity details in Section 4 below. The zoo is in Brackenridge Park (~10 min drive from downtown) and is excellent for both age groups — budget 2.5–3 hours and ~$80–$100 for a family of 4 including parking. Natural Bridge Caverns is ~30 min north of downtown and offers guided cave tours plus an outdoor adventure course — budget 2–3 hours and ~$80–$120 depending on activities. |
| **5:30–6:30 PM** | Return to hotel, rest, pool time. |
| **6:30–8:00 PM** | **Dinner.** If you haven't done Drury Kickback: try **Bill Miller Bar-B-Q** for a cheap, authentically Texan experience ($30–$40 for the family) or **Blaze Pizza** near the Riverwalk for an easy, customizable meal kids love (~$35–$45). If you want a nicer sit-down: **Boudro's** on the Riverwalk (slightly upscale but kids are welcome, excellent guacamole made tableside, ~$80–$100 for the family). |
| **8:00–8:30 PM** | After-dinner walk along the Riverwalk. Get ice cream at **Paletería San Antonio** or any of the gelato shops along the river. |

---

### 📅 April 12 (Saturday) — Adventure Day

**Theme: Unique-to-San-Antonio experiences**

| Time | Activity |
|---|---|
| **8:00–9:00 AM** | Breakfast at hotel. |
| **9:30 AM–1:00 PM** | **Morgan's Wonderland** — the world's first fully accessible theme park, but it's incredible for ALL kids, not just those with special needs. It has a huge splash park (Ultra-Accessible Splash Park), rides, adventure play areas, a fishing pier, and more. It's free for guests with special needs; for general admission, tickets are ~$17/person (kids under 2 free). This place is genuinely wonderful and a hidden gem that most tourists overlook. It's about 15 minutes northeast of downtown. Budget 3+ hours easily. The kids will love it. Pack swimsuits for the splash pad. |
| **1:00–2:00 PM** | Lunch near Morgan's Wonderland or on the way back: grab tacos at a drive-through **Taco Cabana** or **Los Barrios** (a legendary family-run Mexican restaurant, ~$50–$60 for the family, about 5 minutes from Morgan's Wonderland). |
| **2:30–5:00 PM** | **San Antonio Missions National Historical Park.** This is a UNESCO World Heritage Site — a chain of 4 Spanish colonial missions (in addition to the Alamo, which is technically the 5th). **Mission San José** is the most impressive and has the best visitor center. It's free (National Park Service). The 11-year-old will appreciate the history; both kids will enjoy climbing around the old stone structures and the wide-open grounds. Bring water — it can be warm in April. You don't need to see all 4 missions; San José alone is worth the trip (budget 1–1.5 hours). The Mission Reach section of the Riverwalk extends to these missions if you want to walk or bike part of it. |
| **5:00–6:00 PM** | Drive back to hotel, rest, pack partially for tomorrow's checkout. |
| **6:00–7:30 PM** | **Last San Antonio dinner.** Splurge option: **La Gloria** at the Pearl District (chef-driven Mexican street food, incredible flavors, great outdoor seating, kids welcome, ~$70–$90 for the family). Budget option: **Taco Palenque** or street tacos anywhere — you're in San Antonio, and the baseline quality of tacos is extraordinary. |
| **8:00 PM** | Evening Riverwalk stroll for one last look. Ice cream. Hotel. |

---

### 📅 April 13 (Sunday) — Checkout & Drive to Austin

**Theme: One more stop, then hit the road**

| Time | Activity |
|---|---|
| **8:00–9:00 AM** | Breakfast at hotel. Pack up and check out. Load the car. |
| **9:00–10:30 AM** | **The Pearl District.** This is a revitalized brewery complex that's become one of San Antonio's coolest neighborhoods. On Sunday mornings, the **Pearl Farmers Market** runs from 9 AM–1 PM (free to browse). Fresh pastries, local food vendors, live music, and a beautiful setting along the river. Let the kids pick a treat, grab a coffee, and enjoy the vibe. Even if the market timing doesn't work, the Pearl has great shops and a gorgeous walk along the Museum Reach portion of the Riverwalk. Budget 60–90 minutes. |
| **10:30–11:00 AM** | Get on the road. Head north on **I-35** toward Austin. |
| **~11:00 AM–12:30 PM** | **Drive: San Antonio → Austin.** Details in Section 5. |

---

### AUSTIN

---

### 📅 April 13 (Sunday) — Arrival in Austin

**Theme: Settle in, explore the neighborhood**

| Time | Activity |
|---|---|
| **12:30–1:30 PM** | Arrive in Austin. Check into hotel. |
| **1:30–2:30 PM** | **Lunch on South Congress (SoCo).** Walk to South Congress Avenue and grab lunch. Top picks: **Hopdoddy Burger Bar** (gourmet burgers, family-friendly, expect a line but it moves — ~$50–$65 for the family), **Torchy's Tacos** (Austin institution, "damn good tacos," colorful and fun, ~$40–$55), or **Home Slice Pizza** (New York–style pizza, beloved by locals, ~$40–$50). |
| **2:30–4:30 PM** | **Walk South Congress.** This is Austin's signature strip. Must-stops with kids: **Allen's Boots** (enormous wall of cowboy boots — the kids can try some on, it's a photo op even if you don't buy), **Big Top Candy Shop** (an old-fashioned candy store that will make your 8-year-old lose their mind), **Lucy in Disguise with Diamonds** (a costume/vintage shop that's pure fun to browse), and the famous **"Greetings from Austin" mural** (at 1720 S 1st Street, a short detour — great family photo). Also keep an eye out for the "I love you so much" mural on the side of Jo's Coffee. This is a "wander and discover" afternoon. |
| **4:30–5:30 PM** | Return to hotel, rest, pool time. |
| **5:30–7:00 PM** | **Dinner: food trailers!** Austin is the food truck capital of America. The **South Congress food trailers** near the intersection of SoCo and Elizabeth Street have a rotating selection. Or drive 10 minutes to a food truck park like **The Picnic** (on Barton Springs Rd) or **Cosmic Coffee + Beer Garden** (huge outdoor space with play areas, multiple food trucks, and a beautiful garden setting — extremely kid-friendly, adults can have a local craft beer, dinner for the family ~$40–$55). |
| **7:30–8:30 PM** | **Congress Avenue Bridge Bat Colony.** From mid-March through October, approximately **1.5 million Mexican free-tailed bats** emerge from under the Congress Avenue Bridge at dusk. This is one of the most spectacular urban wildlife experiences in North America. In mid-April, sunset is around 7:50–8:00 PM, and bats emerge around 8:00–8:15 PM. Get there by 7:30 to claim a spot on the bridge's east sidewalk or the grassy hill on the south bank (the Statesman Bat Observation Area). It's FREE. The kids will never forget this. The 11-year-old will think it's amazing; the 8-year-old will probably alternate between awe and slight nervousness (the bats don't come near people). You'll see a dark ribbon of bats streaming out from under the bridge against the sunset sky. Genuinely magical. |
| **9:00 PM** | Walk back to hotel. |

---

### 📅 April 14 (Monday) — Museum & Nature Day

**Theme: Learn something, then get outside**

| Time | Activity |
|---|---|
| **8:00–9:00 AM** | Breakfast (hotel or **Jo's Coffee** on SoCo for breakfast tacos and coffee — ~$25–$35 for the family). |
| **9:30 AM–12:00 PM** | **Bullock Texas State History Museum.** Three floors of Texas history, from prehistoric times through the space program. Excellent interactive exhibits, an IMAX theater (check what's showing — nature/space films are perfect for kids), and a "becoming Texas" experience. The 11-year-old will be fully engaged; the 8-year-old will love the hands-on elements and the IMAX. Located downtown on Congress Avenue. Admission: ~$13/adult, ~$9/child (IMAX is extra, ~$8–$10/person). Budget ~$55–$75 for the family including IMAX. |
| **12:00–1:00 PM** | Lunch downtown: **Veracruz All Natural** food truck (some of the best migas and breakfast tacos in the city, even at lunch — ~$30–$40 for the family) or **Easy Tiger** on East 6th (bakery + beer garden on the creek, sandwiches and pretzels, great outdoor space, ~$40–$55). |
| **1:30–4:30 PM** | **Barton Springs Pool.** This is a natural spring-fed swimming pool in Zilker Park. The water is a constant 68°F year-round — refreshing but not freezing in April. It's 3 acres of crystal-clear, spring-fed water in a natural limestone pool setting. Admission is ~$5/adult, ~$3/child (Austin residents less). **This is one of the most unique swimming experiences in America.** The kids can swim, explore the shallow end, and spot the endangered Barton Springs salamander. Bring towels, sunscreen, and snacks. Even if the kids only swim for an hour, the setting in Zilker Park is beautiful for lounging and playing. |
| **4:30–5:30 PM** | **Zilker Park exploration.** After swimming, explore the park. There's a free hillside to run around, a miniature train (**Zilker Eagle**, ~$4/person, 25-minute ride through the park — both kids will enjoy this), and the **Zilker Botanical Garden** adjacent (~$5/person, beautiful in April). |
| **5:30–6:30 PM** | Return to hotel, clean up. |
| **6:30–8:00 PM** | **Dinner: Guero's Taco Bar** on South Congress (lively Tex-Mex, outdoor seating, live music often, great margaritas for the adults, kids' menu — ~$60–$75 for the family). Or **Matt's El Rancho** (legendary Austin Tex-Mex since 1952, the "Bob Armstrong Dip" is famous, family-friendly, ~$60–$80). |

---

### 📅 April 15 (Tuesday) — Outdoors & Weird Austin

**Theme: Keep Austin Weird**

| Time | Activity |
|---|---|
| **8:00–9:00 AM** | Breakfast at hotel. |
| **9:00 AM–12:00 PM** | **Lady Bird Lake Kayaking/Paddleboarding.** Rent kayaks or stand-up paddleboards at one of the lakeside rental shops. **Texas Rowing Center** or **Rowing Dock** are good options. Single kayaks ~$15–$20/hour, double kayaks ~$25–$30/hour. The 8 and 11-year-old can share a double with an adult or, depending on comfort level, paddle their own sit-on-top kayak (they're very stable). The lake is calm — no motorized boats allowed. You'll paddle past downtown Austin's skyline, under bridges, and through gorgeous tree-lined sections. Morning is best before it gets warm. Budget ~$60–$80 for the family for 1.5–2 hours. |
| **12:00–1:00 PM** | **Lunch: Loro** (Asian smokehouse by the teams behind Franklin Barbecue and Uchi — smoked brisket Thai rice, coconut curry, etc. — ~$50–$70 for the family, outdoor seating, great for adventurous eaters) OR **P. Terry's Burger Stand** (Austin's beloved fast-food burger chain, local equivalent of In-N-Out — ~$25–$35 for the family, fast and delicious). |
| **1:30–3:30 PM** | **Austin Nature & Science Center** (in Zilker Park, FREE admission, donations encouraged). This is a hidden gem — rescued animals exhibit (birds of prey, reptiles, mammals), a dino dig pit for younger kids, nature trails, and hands-on science exhibits. The 8-year-old especially will love the animals. Then walk over to the **Zilker Park Playscape** — one of Austin's best playgrounds, with climbing structures and creative play areas. |
| **3:30–4:30 PM** | **Drive down to the "Cathedral of Junk"** (if it's open — check ahead, it's in a private backyard and visits are by appointment/text: Google "Cathedral of Junk Austin" for the current phone number). It's a 3-story sculpture made entirely of junk — bikes, signs, toys, car parts — in a guy's backyard. It's been there since 1988. Free to visit (donation of ~$5 appreciated). This is "Keep Austin Weird" incarnate. The kids will be amazed. If it's not available, substitute with the **HOPE Outdoor Gallery** (Austin's famous graffiti park) — note: the original location on Baylor Street closed, but a new community art park may be operational. Check current status before going. Alternative: drive by some of Austin's famous murals for photo ops. |
| **5:00–6:00 PM** | Hotel, rest. |
| **6:00–8:00 PM** | **Dinner: Pinthouse Pizza** (Austin-brewed craft beer for adults, excellent pizza, very family-friendly atmosphere, ~$50–$65 for the family). Or if you want to try Austin's BBQ scene without the hours-long Franklin Barbecue line: **la Barbecue** or **Micklethwait Craft Meats** (both on the east side, both have shorter lines than Franklin, both are phenomenal — expect ~$60–$80 for the family for brisket, ribs, sides, and drinks. Go at 5:30 to avoid selling out). |

---

### 📅 April 16 (Wednesday) — Last Full Austin Day

**Theme: Round Rock day trip + farewell Austin evening**

| Time | Activity |
|---|---|
| **8:00–9:00 AM** | Breakfast at hotel. |
| **9:30 AM–1:00 PM** | **Inner Space Cavern** (in Georgetown, ~30 min north of Austin). A fantastic cave discovered during highway construction in 1963. Guided tours take you through illuminated caverns with stalactites, stalagmites, and even Ice Age animal bones. Adventure tours are available for older kids. Standard tours: ~$15–$20/adult, ~$10–$13/child. The constant 72°F inside the cave feels great. Budget 1.5–2 hours. **Alternative:** If you did Natural Bridge Caverns in San Antonio, swap this for **Round Rock Donuts** (famous for their giant, bright orange Texas-sized donuts — the kids will love it) and **Rock'N River Family Aquatic Center** in Round Rock (a water park with a lazy river, water slides, and a wave pool — check if it's open in April, as some outdoor aquatic centers don't open until May). If that's closed, do the **Thinkery** instead (see below). |
| **1:00–2:00 PM** | Lunch in Georgetown or Round Rock: **Rudy's Country Store & Bar-B-Q** (a Texas BBQ chain that's actually good — gas station aesthetic, meat sold by the pound, sausage and brisket and cream corn — ~$50–$65 for the family). |
| **2:30–5:00 PM** | **Thinkery (Austin's Children's Museum).** Located in the Mueller neighborhood. This is a hands-on STEAM museum designed for kids exactly your children's ages. Highlights: outdoor kitchen garden, an enormous water play area (bring a change of clothes), a maker space where kids build with real tools, and rotating science exhibits. Admission: ~$14/person. The 8-year-old could happily spend 3 hours here; the 11-year-old will gravitate to the maker/engineering challenges. This is one of the best children's museums in the Southwest. |
| **5:00–6:00 PM** | Back to hotel. Pack bags. |
| **6:00–8:00 PM** | **Farewell Austin Dinner.** Make this one special. **Oasis Texas Brewing Company** ("The Sunset Capital of Texas") — perched on a cliff 450 feet above Lake Travis with a massive multi-tiered deck overlooking the lake. ## 4. Kid-Friendly Activities — Top 5 Must-Do in Each City

### San Antonio Top 5

| # | Activity | Why It's Great | Ages 8–11 Appeal | Cost (family of 4) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **The Alamo + Museum** | It's THE Texas landmark. The new museum brings history alive with interactive exhibits, weapons, artifacts, and multimedia storytelling. Standing where the battle happened is powerful. | 11-yr-old: high (history is engaging). 8-yr-old: medium-high (cannons, swords, the "fort" atmosphere). | Free (timed tickets required; reserve online) |
| **2** | **Riverwalk Boat Cruise (Rio San Antonio)** | A gentle, narrated 35-minute cruise along the Riverwalk. You pass under stone bridges, past restaurants, through a quiet stretch with herons and turtles, and get a history of the river. It's relaxing and the kids love being on the water. Best at dusk when the lights come on. | Both ages: high. Being on a boat is inherently fun. | ~$35–$45 |
| **3** | **San Antonio Zoo** | 750+ species, a well-designed layout in historic Brackenridge Park. Highlights: the catfish feeding at the river (kids can buy food pellets), the Africa Live! exhibit, the butterfly garden, and the train ride through the park. Not as overwhelming as mega-zoos — you can do it in 2.5–3 hours. | Both ages: high. | ~$80–$100 (tickets + parking) |
| **4** | **Natural Bridge Caverns** | The largest commercial cavern in Texas. The Discovery Tour takes you 180 feet below ground through massive chambers with stunning formations. Temperature is a constant 70°F. The outdoor area has gem mining, a ropes course, a maze, and zip lines (extra cost). The combination of underground wonder + outdoor adventure makes this a full half-day. | 11-yr-old: very high (adventure + science). 8-yr-old: high (it's a real cave!). | ~$80–$130 (depending on activities chosen) |
| **5** | **Morgan's Wonderland / Market Square** | Morgan's Wonderland is a 25-acre accessible theme park with rides, a splash park, and adventure areas. It's joyful and uncrowded compared to commercial theme parks. Market Square (El Mercado) is a different kind of fun — colorful, cultural, full of things to see and touch. Together they represent the spectrum of San Antonio kid experiences. | Both ages: high for Morgan's Wonderland. Market Square is better for the 11-yr-old (shopping/browsing) but the 8-yr-old will love the colors and treats. | Morgan's: ~$70. Market Square: free to browse, budget $20–$30 for treats/small souvenirs. |

### Austin Top 5

| # | Activity | Why It's Great | Ages 8–11 Appeal | Cost (family of 4) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **Congress Avenue Bridge Bat Colony** | 1.5 million bats erupting from under a bridge at sunset is one of the most astonishing natural spectacles you can witness in any American city. It's free, it happens every evening March–October, and your family will talk about it for years. | Both ages: very high. This is "wow" factor at its purest. | Free |
| **2** | **Barton Springs Pool** | A 3-acre natural spring-fed pool with constant 68°F crystal-clear water, set in beautiful Zilker Park. It's unlike any swimming pool your kids have ever been in — it's a natural limestone creek bed. They can spot fish and salamanders. It's quintessentially Austin. | Both ages: very high (swimming is swimming, and this is special swimming). | ~$16 |
| **3** | **Thinkery (Children's Museum)** | Hands-on STEAM museum with an outdoor water play area, maker space, kitchen garden, and rotating exhibits designed for exactly the 5–12 age range. It's modern, well-designed, and engaging. Not your grandmother's children's museum. | 8-yr-old: very high. 11-yr-old: high (gravitates to engineering/maker challenges). | ~$56 |
| **4** | **Kayaking/Paddleboarding Lady Bird Lake** | Paddling on a calm lake with the Austin skyline as your backdrop. No motorized boats allowed, so it's safe and peaceful. Kids can paddle their own sit-on-top kayak (they're very stable) or share a tandem with a parent. Turtles, herons, and sometimes even river otters. | Both ages: high. Physical activity + being on the water + a sense of independence for the 11-yr-old if they paddle solo. | ~$60–$80 |
| **5** | **South Congress Avenue (SoCo) Walk** | This isn't a single "activity" — it's an experience. Cowboy boot shopping at Allen's Boots, candy at Big Top Candy Shop, vintage costumes at Lucy in Disguise, famous murals for photos, food trailers, and ice cream at Amy's. It's walkable, colorful, and captures the spirit of Austin. Your kids will feel like they're somewhere truly unique. | 8-yr-old: high (candy shop, ice cream, costumes). 11-yr-old: high (boots, murals, the general "cool" factor of SoCo). | Free to walk; budget $20–$40 for candy, ice cream, small purchases. |

**Honorable mentions:** Bullock Texas State History Museum (IMAX!), Austin Nature & Science Center (free!), Mount Bonnell (short hike, incredible view of Lake Austin — 102 steps to the top, both kids can handle it, free), and Inner Space Cavern (if you didn't do Natural Bridge in SA).

## 5. Driving Routes

### Route 1: San Antonio → Austin

| Detail | Info |
|---|---|
| **Route** | I-35 North |
| **Distance** | ~80 miles |
| **Drive time** | 1 hour 15 minutes – 1 hour 40 minutes (depending on traffic) |
| **Traffic notes** | I-35 through San Marcos and Kyle can get congested, especially on weekends. Sunday midday (your drive day) is usually moderate. Construction on I-35 is perpetual in Texas — expect some construction zones. Use Google Maps or Waze for real-time routing. |
| **Fuel** | You won't need to stop for gas on this short drive, but top off in San Antonio before departing. Gas prices in Texas are generally $2.80–$3.50/gallon (significantly cheaper than Seattle). |

**Worth-a-stop options:**

- **San Marcos Premium Outlets** (exit 200 on I-35, about 45 min into the drive). One of the largest outlet malls in Texas. Only stop if you're specifically looking for deals — it can be a time sink. Not recommended with kids who just want to arrive.

- **Buc-ee's (New Braunfels)** — THIS IS THE STOP. If your family has never experienced a Buc-ee's, it is a **mandatory Texas experience.** It's a gas station the size of a department store. We're talking 60,000+ square feet with 120 fuel pumps, an entire wall of beef jerky, freshly made brisket sandwiches, fudge, beaver nuggets (addictive sweet corn puff snacks), a bakery, an absurd selection of snacks, clean bathrooms (famously the cleanest gas station bathrooms in America), and Buc-ee's branded merchandise (t-shirts, stuffed beavers, cups). Your kids will think they've entered Willy Wonka's gas station. Located at exit 191 on I-35 in New Braunfels, about 30 minutes north of San Antonio. Budget 20–30 minutes and $15–$25 for snacks (you will buy snacks, resistance is futile). This is easily the best road trip stop in Texas and your kids will remember it.

- **Gruene Historic District** (exit 191 or 189, then a short drive west — same exit area as Buc-ee's). A tiny, preserved German-Texas town with **Gruene Hall** (the oldest dance hall in Texas, open since 1878 — you can pop in briefly even with kids during the day), antique shops, and the **Gristmill Restaurant** overlooking the Guadalupe River. This is a charming 30–45 minute stop if you want to stretch your legs in a beautiful setting. Only do this if you have time and aren't in a rush to get to Austin.

---

### Route 2: Austin → Houston (Hobby Airport)

| Detail | Info |
|---|---|
| **Route** | TX-71 East → I-10 East → TX-288 South / I-45 South (to Hobby area). Or: US-290 East → I-610 to Hobby. Google Maps will optimize based on traffic. |
| **Distance** | ~165 miles |
| **Drive time** | 2 hours 30 minutes – 3 hours 15 minutes |
| **Traffic notes** | **Houston traffic is real.** If you're arriving in Houston between 7–9 AM or 4–7 PM, add 30–60 minutes. Arriving midday (your plan) should be manageable. I-10 coming into Houston from the west can bottleneck. Waze is essential. |
| **Fuel** | Fill up in Austin before departing. You'll have plenty of fuel to reach Houston, but there's a Buc-ee's in Katy (west Houston) if you want one last stop: **Buc-ee's Katy**, right off I-10, is one of their flagships. If you already stopped at the New Braunfels one, you don't need another — but the kids might beg. |

**Worth-a-stop options:**

- **Buc-ee's Luling** (on US-183, slightly off the most direct route but only a few minutes' detour if you're taking 183/I-10). Or **Buc-ee's Katy** (on I-10, right before you enter Houston proper).

- **Hruska's Bakery & Deli in Ellinger** (if taking US-71/TX-71 to I-10). A classic Czech-Texan roadside bakery famous for kolaches (Czech pastries filled with sausage, cheese, fruit, etc.). Kolaches are a Texas road trip tradition. Quick stop, $10–$15 for a bag of kolaches.

- **If taking US-290:** You'll pass through **Brenham**, home of **Blue Bell Creameries**. The "Blue Bell Factory Tour" is popular but may require advance booking. Even without a tour, the **Blue Bell Ice Cream Parlor** in Brenham is worth a 15-minute stop for fresh scoops of Texas's most beloved ice cream brand. Your kids get Seattle's Salt & Straw — wait until they try Blue Bell's Homemade Vanilla and The Great Divide.

## 7. Practical Tips

### Best Apps for Road Trips with Kids

| App | Why |
|---|---|
| **Waze** | Real-time traffic, police alerts, construction zones. Essential for Houston driving. |
| **Google Maps** (offline maps) | Download Texas maps for offline use in case you lose cell signal in rural stretches between Austin and Houston. |
| **GasBuddy** | Find cheapest gas near you. Less critical in Texas (gas is cheap everywhere) but still useful. |
| **Roadtrippers** | Plot your route and discover quirky stops, restaurants, and attractions along the way. |
| **AllTrails** | If you want a quick hike anywhere along the route (Mount Bonnell in Austin, for example). |
| **Buc-ee's app** | Yes, it exists. Find locations, see what's in stock. Your kids will want this after the first visit. |
| **Libby / Spotify / Audible** | Download audiobooks and playlists BEFORE the trip. Recommendations for the car: *The Wild Robot* by Peter Brown (audiobook, perfect for ages 8–11), *Hatchet* by Gary Paulsen, or the *Percy Jackson* series if they haven't listened yet. |

### What to Pack in the Car

| Item | Why |
|---|---|
| **Refillable water bottles (×4)** | Texas in April can hit 80–85°F. Hydration is critical at outdoor activities, especially Barton Springs, the zoo, and the Missions. |
| **Sunscreen (SPF 50+)** | Texas sun is strong, even in April. Seattle families are often caught off guard. |
| **Hats and sunglasses** | See above. |
| **Swimsuits & towels** | Barton Springs, Morgan's Wonderland splash pad, hotel pools. Have these accessible, not buried in the trunk. |
| **Small cooler or insulated bag** | Fill with drinks, cheese sticks, fruit, and sandwich supplies from H-E-B. This saves money and prevents hangry meltdowns between activities. |
| **Car phone charger (dual USB)** | Two adults, two kids, potentially 4 devices needing juice. |
| **Portable battery pack** | For the bat viewing evening — your phone will be at 12% from navigating and photographing all day. |
| **Light jackets or hoodies** | April mornings and evenings in San Antonio/Austin can dip to 55–65°F. Also useful inside the 68°F Barton Springs Pool area and the 70°F caves. |
| **Rain jacket or poncho** | April is part of Texas's spring storm season. Quick afternoon thunderstorms are possible. They're usually brief but intense. |
| **First aid kit** | Band-aids, Benadryl, ibuprofen, anti-itch cream. Outdoor activities + kids = minor scrapes. |
| **Entertainment bag** | Headphones (×2 for kids), tablets or a shared iPad loaded with downloaded shows/movies, a few card games (Uno, Spot It), coloring book/colored pencils for the 8-yr-old. The Austin→Houston drive is the longest at 2.5–3 hours. |
| **Ziplock bags** | Wet swimsuits, leftover snacks, collecting rocks/treasures, keeping phones dry. The most underrated road trip item. |
| **Paper towels / wet wipes** | BBQ is messy. Tacos are messy. Kids are messy. Texas is messy (in the best way). |

### April-Specific Events & Festivals

| Event | City | Dates | Details |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Fiesta San Antonio** | San Antonio | Typically mid-to-late April (check fiestacommission.com for 2025 dates) | ⚠️ **This is huge.** If your dates overlap with Fiesta, expect higher hotel prices, more crowds, but also an incredible, once-a-year cultural festival. Parades, food, music, cascarones (confetti eggs). If it overlaps with April 10–13, embrace it — it's an amazing experience for kids. But book hotels NOW. |
| **Wildflower season** | Between San Antonio & Austin (especially along I-35 and US-290) | March–April | **Texas bluebonnets** should be in full bloom in mid-April. Watch for fields of blue along the highway. Pull over (carefully) at any safe shoulder with wildflowers for the quintessential Texas family photo. The kids standing in a field of bluebonnets with the Texas sky behind them is the photo you'll frame. Popular spots: along I-35 near Ennis/Temple, or drive the **Willow City Loop** (northwest of Austin) if you have a spare half-day. |
| **Austin Reggae Festival** | Austin (Zilker Park) | Typically mid-April weekend | A laid-back music festival in Zilker Park. Family-friendly during daytime. Check dates — if it falls on your Austin weekend, the park area will be busy but festive. |
| **Rodeo Austin** | Austin | Usually March (might extend into early April) | If it's still running, the rodeo events, carnival rides, and livestock shows are very kid-friendly. Check rodeoaustin.com for exact dates. |
| **Moontower Comedy Festival** | Austin | Sometimes mid-April | Stand-up comedy festival. Not directly kid-relevant but worth knowing about if adults want to catch a show (some daytime shows are appropriate for older kids). |

> **Key alert: Fiesta San Antonio.** Check the 2025 dates immediately. In many years, Fiesta falls in the second or third week of April, which could directly overlap with your April 10–13 stay. If it does: (a) hotel prices in San Antonio could be 50–100% higher, (b) you should attend a Fiesta event — it's genuinely spectacular, and (c) book your hotel immediately.
